proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a sufficiently large index \(n\), a revealed simple \(d\)-regular graph \(G\), and a fixed schedule \(y\in\mathcal M_2(G)\).  Let \(T_{\mathrm{CG}}\) denote the modified Horvitz--Thompson estimator computed with the internal desired-exposure variables of the published Conflict Graph Design.  The cited result \(\text{lem:published-conflict-graph-risk}\) gives
\[
\mathbb E(T_{\mathrm{CG}}\mid G)=\tau_G(y) \tag{9}
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{Var}(T_{\mathrm{CG}}\mid G)
\le \frac{12.5\|B_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{n}
\left\{\frac1n\sum_{i\in V}y_{i1}^2+
\frac1n\sum_{i\in V}y_{i0}^2\right\}. \tag{10}
\]
The frozen minimax class permits estimators based on \((G,Z,y(Z))\), not hidden design metadata.  Define the observed-data version
\[
T_{\mathrm{CG}}^{\mathrm{RB}}
=\mathbb E[T_{\mathrm{CG}}\mid G,Z,y(Z)]. \tag{11}
\]
This is one common, data-driven map rather than a schedule-specific oracle.  Indeed, all spaces are finite, the joint law of the internal desired-exposure variables \(U\) and \(Z\) is fixed by \(G\), and \(T_{\mathrm{CG}}\) depends on the schedule only through \(y(Z)\).  Thus, for every realized pair \((z,Y)\), (11) is the same design-known finite sum
\[
T_{\mathrm{CG}}^{\mathrm{RB}}(G,z,Y)
=\sum_u T_{\mathrm{CG}}(G,z,Y,u)\Pr_G\{U=u\mid Z=z\},
\]
with an arbitrary value assigned on zero-probability assignments.  Hence it is a measurable function of the permitted observed data for every schedule in the class.  The tower property and (9) imply
\[
\mathbb E(T_{\mathrm{CG}}^{\mathrm{RB}}\mid G)
=\mathbb E(T_{\mathrm{CG}}\mid G)=\tau_G(y). \tag{12}
\]
The law of total variance gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}(T_{\mathrm{CG}}\mid G)
=\operatorname{Var}(T_{\mathrm{CG}}^{\mathrm{RB}}\mid G)
+\mathbb E\!\left[\operatorname{Var}(T_{\mathrm{CG}}\mid G,Z,y(Z))\mid G\right], \tag{13}
\]
so the second nonnegative term shows that Rao--Blackwellization cannot increase variance.

By \(\text{def:endpoint-class}\), the two endpoint second moments in braces in (10) are separately at most one.  Combining (10)--(13) and using unbiasedness yields, uniformly over \(y\in\mathcal M_2(G)\),
\[
\mathbb E[(T_{\mathrm{CG}}^{\mathrm{RB}}-\tau_G)^2\mid G]
=\operatorname{Var}(T_{\mathrm{CG}}^{\mathrm{RB}}\mid G)
\le\frac{25\|B_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{n}. \tag{14}
\]
The proved spectral identification \(\text{lem:gate-conflict-spectral-map}\) changes (14) into
\[
\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_2(G)}
\mathbb E[(T_{\mathrm{CG}}^{\mathrm{RB}}-\tau_G)^2\mid G]
\le\frac{25\lambda(H_G)}{n}
\le\frac{25(1+d^2)}{n}. \tag{15}
\]
Assumption \(\text{ass:degree-diverges}\) implies that eventually \(d\ge1\), and then \(1+d^2\le2d^2\).  Thus (15) is at most \(50d^2/n\).

The Conflict Graph Design depends only on \(G\), and (11) is an observed-data measurable estimator; hence this pair is admissible in the infimum of \(\text{def:minimax-risk}\).  Evaluating that infimum at this one pair and applying (15) proves
\[
R_2(G)\le
\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_2(G)}
\mathbb E[(T_{\mathrm{CG}}^{\mathrm{RB}}-\tau_G)^2\mid G]
\le\frac{50d^2}{n}. \tag{16}
\]
The bound is deterministic for every revealed simple \(d\)-regular \(G\) once \(d\ge1\); therefore it holds, a fortiori, with probability \(1-o(1)\) under \(G_n\).  Assumption \(\text{ass:subsqrt-degree}\) specifies the common regime in which this upper bound is paired with the frozen lower theorem, although it is not needed for the finite-graph inequality (16).

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose that \(\pi_u>0\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\).  For \(a,b\in\{0,1\}\), define the \(V\)-by-\(V\) block
\[
K_{ab}(i,j)=\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(
 \frac{X_{(i,a)}}{\pi_{(i,a)}},
 \frac{X_{(j,b)}}{\pi_{(j,b)}}\,\middle|\,G\right).
\]
Then \(\Gamma_G\) is positive semidefinite and, in the arm order \((1,0)\),
\[
\Gamma_G=
\begin{pmatrix}
K_{11}&-K_{10}\\
-K_{01}&K_{00}
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
(\Gamma_G)_{uu}=\pi_u^{-1}-1,
\qquad
\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \ge \max_{u\in\mathcal U}(\pi_u^{-1}-1).
\]
If \(a\ne b\) and \(\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)\le2\), then
\((\Gamma_G)_{(i,a),(j,b)}=1\).  Moreover, on every realization of the capped design,
\[
\sum_{i\in V}X_{(i,1)}=\sum_{i\in V}X_{(i,0)}.
\]
Consequently, if all \(\pi_u\) have one common positive value, the all-ones vector belongs to the kernel of \(\Gamma_G\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Condition throughout on the revealed graph \(G\).  Put \(W_u=X_u/\pi_u\), and let \(D\) be the diagonal matrix indexed by \(\mathcal U\) with \(D_{uu}=s_a\) for \(u=(i,a)\).  The definition \(\text{def:normalized-kernel}\) gives, entry by entry,
\[
\Gamma_G=D\operatorname{Cov}(W\mid G)D. \tag{1}
\]
For every deterministic vector \(q\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal U}\),
\[
q^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_Gq
=(Dq)^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{Cov}(W\mid G)(Dq)
=\operatorname{Var}\!\left((Dq)^{\mathsf T}W\mid G\right)\ge0, \tag{2}
\]
so \(\Gamma_G\) is positive semidefinite.  Splitting (1) by arm and using \(s_1=1\) and \(s_0=-1\) gives exactly
\[
\Gamma_G=\begin{pmatrix}K_{11}&-K_{10}\\-K_{01}&K_{00}\end{pmatrix}. \tag{3}
\]
Because each \(X_u\) is Bernoulli with conditional mean \(\pi_u\),
\[
(\Gamma_G)_{uu}
=s_a^2\operatorname{Var}(X_u/\pi_u\mid G)
=\frac{\pi_u(1-\pi_u)}{\pi_u^2}
=\pi_u^{-1}-1. \tag{4}
\]
The Rayleigh quotient at the coordinate vector \(e_u\), together with (2), now yields
\[
\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\ge e_u^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_Ge_u
=\pi_u^{-1}-1,
\]
and maximizing over \(u\) proves the diagonal lower bound.

Consider next \(a\ne b\) and \(\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)\le2\).  On an accepted trial, \(C\subseteq F_G(A)\) by \(\text{def:reservoir-capsule}\), so no element of \(A\) is within distance two of an element of \(C\).  The arm swap merely exchanges \(A\) and \(C\).  Hence \(X_{(i,a)}X_{(j,b)}=0\) on an accepted trial.  On the capped fallback every \(X_u\) is zero, so the same equality holds.  Positivity of the two inclusion probabilities therefore permits division and gives
\[
\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(\frac{X_{(i,a)}}{\pi_{(i,a)}},
\frac{X_{(j,b)}}{\pi_{(j,b)}}\,\middle|\,G\right)
=\frac{0}{\pi_{(i,a)}\pi_{(j,b)}}-1=-1. \tag{5}
\]
Since \(s_as_b=-1\), (5) implies \((\Gamma_G)_{(i,a),(j,b)}=1\).

Every accepted realization has \(|T|=|C_0|=k\), while every fallback realization has both focal totals equal to zero.  Thus
\[
\sum_iX_{(i,1)}-\sum_iX_{(i,0)}=0 \quad\text{pathwise}. \tag{6}
\]
If \(\pi_u=\pi>0\) for all \(u\), (6) says that
\[
\sum_{u=(i,a)}s_aW_u=0 \quad\text{pathwise}. \tag{7}
\]
Taking the covariance of each coordinate of \(DW\) with the scalar in (7) proves \(\Gamma_G\mathbf 1=0\), which is the asserted constant-mode cancellation.

The smallest noninterference check is exact.  When \(n=4\) and \(d=0\), one has \(k=1\); the capsule selects a uniformly ordered pair of distinct focal units and assigns its two members to opposite arms.  Hence every \(\pi_u=1/4\).  The diagonal entries of \(\Gamma_G\) are \(3\); distinct same-arm entries are \(-1\); same-unit cross-arm entries are \(1\); and distinct cross-arm entries are \(-1/3\).  Every row therefore sums to
\[
3+3(-1)+1+3(-1/3)=0,
\]
confirming (3)--(7) by complete enumeration in the smallest admissible instance.  At the opposite finite boundary, \(G=K_4\) has no accepted reservoir pair and all \(\pi_u=0\), confirming that the positivity premise cannot be omitted from the normalized-kernel identities.
added_lemmas.justification: This finite-design lemma separates the capsule identities that are exact from the unresolved random-regular operator upper bound.
added_lemmas.gap: Positive semidefiniteness, diagonal scale, incompatible-pair entries, and constant-mode cancellation do not control the heterogeneous compatible-pair block after reservoir acceptance conditioning.
added_lemmas.consumer: The capsule-kernel conjecture records these identities as its proved presolve capsule.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(B\) be a symmetric zero--one conflict matrix on \(V\) with diagonal entries one, let \(\Lambda=\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), and let \(\sigma\) be an importance ordering.  Write \(M_\sigma(i)\) for the conflict neighbors of \(i\) preceding it in \(\sigma\).  In the Conflict Graph Design with sampling parameter \(\rho>1\), let \(E_{i,a}\) denote the event that unit \(i\) requests endpoint arm \(a\) and every member of \(M_\sigma(i)\) requests the null option.  Then
\[
\Pr(E_{i,a})=\frac{1}{2\rho\Lambda}
\left(1-\frac{1}{\rho\Lambda}\right)^{|M_\sigma(i)|}.
\]
For distinct \(i,j\), \(\Pr(E_{i,a}\cap E_{j,b})=0\) when \(B_{ij}=1\), and otherwise
\[
\Pr(E_{i,a}\cap E_{j,b})=\frac{1}{(2\rho\Lambda)^2}
\left(1-\frac{1}{\rho\Lambda}\right)^{|M_\sigma(i)\cup M_\sigma(j)|}.
\]

attestation.note: Verified against the full statement of Lemma 3.3 in the arXiv v3 HTML source.

added_lemmas.statement:
Under the Conflict Graph Design with sampling parameter two, let \(B\), \(\Lambda\), \(\sigma\), and \(E_{i,a}\) be as in the design's conflict-matrix construction.  Then
\[
\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\frac{\mathbf 1\{E_{i,a}\}}{\Pr(E_{i,a})}\right)\le5\Lambda.
\]
For distinct \(i,j\), the covariance of the two normalized desired-exposure indicators is \(-1\) when their conflict-graph distance is one and is zero when that distance is at least three.  When their distance is two, its absolute value is at most
\[
\frac{6}{\Lambda}\,
\bigl|\{\ell\in V:B_{i\ell}=B_{j\ell}=1\}\bigr|.
\]

attestation.note: Verified against the variance and three distance cases in Lemma 4.2 of the arXiv v3 HTML source.

added_lemmas.statement:
For the global endpoint contrast under arbitrary neighborhood interference, let \(B_G\) be the \(V\)-by-\(V\) matrix with \((B_G)_{ij}=\mathbf 1\{\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)\le2\}\) and let \(\Lambda_G=\|B_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).  The published Conflict Graph Design is outcome-independent and its modified Horvitz--Thompson estimator, including the design's desired-exposure metadata, is unbiased for \(\tau_G\) and satisfies
\[
\operatorname{Var}(T_{\mathrm{CG}}\mid G)
\le \frac{12.5\Lambda_G}{n}
\left\{\frac1n\sum_{i\in V}y_{i1}^2+
\frac1n\sum_{i\in V}y_{i0}^2\right\}.
\]

attestation.note: Verified against Proposition 3.5 for unbiasedness and Theorem 4.1 for the constant-12.5 finite-sample variance inequality in the arXiv v3 HTML source.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every simple \(d\)-regular graph \(G\), define \(B_G\) by \((B_G)_{ij}=\mathbf 1\{\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)\le2\}\).  This is the unit-level conflict matrix for the global endpoint contrast, while the adjacency matrix of \(H_G\) is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}0&B_G\\B_G&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\lambda(H_G)=\|B_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le1+d^2.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(i,j\in V\).  If \(\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)\le2\), then the closed neighborhoods \(N_G[i]\) and \(N_G[j]\) intersect.  Requiring the treated endpoint at \(i\) forces every unit in the first closed neighborhood to treatment, whereas requiring the control endpoint at \(j\) forces every unit in the second closed neighborhood to control.  The two requirements are therefore incompatible.  If \(\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)>2\), the two closed neighborhoods are disjoint, so any requested pair of endpoint arms can be realized by assigning the two neighborhoods separately.  Thus the unit-level global-endpoint conflict relation is exactly \((B_G)_{ij}=1\).

By \(\text{def:gate-conflict-graph}\), edges of \(H_G\) occur only between opposite-arm copies and follow precisely this relation.  Its adjacency matrix therefore has the displayed block form.  Since \(B_G\) is real symmetric, an eigenpair \(B_Gx=\mu x\) produces eigenpairs
\[
\begin{pmatrix}0&B_G\\B_G&0\end{pmatrix}
\binom{x}{x}=\mu\binom{x}{x},
\qquad
\begin{pmatrix}0&B_G\\B_G&0\end{pmatrix}
\binom{x}{-x}=-\mu\binom{x}{-x}.
\]
Hence the spectral radius of the block matrix is \(\|B_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), proving the equality with \(\lambda(H_G)\).

Finally, from a fixed vertex there are at most \(1\) vertices at distance zero, \(d\) at distance one, and \(d(d-1)\) at distance two.  Every row sum of \(B_G\) is thus at most
\[
1+d+d(d-1)=1+d^2. \tag{8}
\]
For a symmetric matrix, the operator norm is at most the maximum absolute row sum; applying this elementary induced-norm inequality to the nonnegative matrix \(B_G\) and using (8) proves \(\|B_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le1+d^2\).  As finite boundary checks, \(d=0\) gives \(B_G=I_n\) and equality \(\|B_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1\), while \(G=K_4\) gives \(B_G\) equal to the all-ones matrix and \(\|B_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}=4\le1+3^2\).
added_lemmas.justification: This lemma identifies the spectral quantity in the published unit-level GATE design with the frozen two-copy comparator and bounds it deterministically on regular graphs.
added_lemmas.gap: The mapping supplies the published \(O(d^2/n)\) upper rate but contains no logarithmic covariance improvement.
added_lemmas.consumer: The published-design upper theorem uses it to convert Theorem 4.1 into a degree-explicit minimax bound.

added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By the already established theorem \(\text{thm:all-procedure-lower}\), there is a universal \(c>0\) and events \(L_n\), measurable with respect to \(G_n\), such that
\[
\Pr_{G_n}(L_n)\to1,
\qquad
R_2(G)\ge c r(n,d)quad\text{on }L_n. \tag{17}
\]
The retargeted upper theorem \(\text{thm:capsule-upper}\) supplies a universal \(C<\infty\) and, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
R_2(G)\le C\frac{d^2}{n} \tag{18}
\]
for every revealed simple \(d\)-regular \(G\).  In particular, if \(U_n\) denotes the event in (18), then \(\Pr_{G_n}(U_n)=1\) eventually.  Therefore
\[
\Pr_{G_n}(L_n\cap U_n)
\ge1-\Pr_{G_n}(L_n^{\mathsf c})-\Pr_{G_n}(U_n^{\mathsf c})
\longrightarrow1. \tag{19}
\]
On the intersection, (17), (18), and \(\text{def:frontier-scale}\) give
\[
c\frac{(d+1)^2}{n\log(d+2)}
=c r(n,d)\le R_2(G)\le C\frac{d^2}{n}. \tag{20}
\]
This proves the probability statement.  Finally, the ratio of the displayed upper endpoint to the lower endpoint is
\[
\frac{Cd^2/n}{c(d+1)^2/[n\log(d+2)]}
=\frac{C}{c}\frac{d^2}{(d+1)^2}\log(d+2)
=\Theta(\log(d+2))
\]
under \(d\to\infty\).  Thus the proved result is precisely a logarithmic-width bracket, and no equality of the two rates follows.
added_lemmas.justification: This is the honest random-regular full-GATE conclusion after preserving the all-procedure lower bound and importing the published conflict-graph upper bound.
added_lemmas.gap: The two endpoints differ by a factor of order \(\log(d+2)\); no available proof shows that the capsule or any other procedure attains the lower endpoint.
added_lemmas.consumer: Experimenters obtain a rigorous degree-explicit minimax bracket, with the distinction between the necessary lower scale and the published sufficient upper scale kept explicit.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Whenever all focal inclusion probabilities are positive, the capsule kernel has the exact decomposition
\[
\Gamma_G=
\begin{pmatrix}K_{11}&-K_{10}\\-K_{01}&K_{00}\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
\qquad
(\Gamma_G)_{uu}=\pi_u^{-1}-1,
\qquad
\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\ge\max_u(\pi_u^{-1}-1),
\]
where \(K_{ab}(i,j)=\operatorname{Cov}(X_{(i,a)}/\pi_{(i,a)},X_{(j,b)}/\pi_{(j,b)}\mid G)\).  Its incompatible opposite-arm entries equal \(1\), and equality of the two focal arm totals makes the all-ones vector a null vector when the inclusion probabilities are uniform.  It remains a conjecture whether there are universal constants \(c,C>0\) such that, uniformly along every sequence with \(d\to\infty\) and \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), with probability \(1-o(1)\) over \(G_n\),
\[
p_{\mathrm{acc}}(G)\ge1-n^{-4},
\qquad
c\frac{k}{n}\le\min_{u\in\mathcal U}\pi_u
\le\max_{u\in\mathcal U}\pi_u\le C\frac{k}{n},
\qquad
\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C\frac{n}{k}.
\]
No \(O(n/k)\) capsule norm bound is asserted as proved.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The asserted \(O(n/k)\) operator upper bound is the unresolved novel crux. The corrected conjecture retains every exact covariance identity proved by the presolve capsule but no longer presents the acceptance, overlap, or norm bounds as a theorem.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
There is a universal constant \(C<\infty\) such that, uniformly along every sequence satisfying \(d\to\infty\) and \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), for every sufficiently large \(n\) and every revealed simple \(d\)-regular graph \(G\), the published Conflict Graph Design followed by observed-data Rao--Blackwellization gives an outcome-independent design and measurable estimator \(T_{\mathrm{CG}}^{\mathrm{RB}}\) satisfying
\[
\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_2(G)}
\mathbb E\!\left[(T_{\mathrm{CG}}^{\mathrm{RB}}-\tau_G)^2\mid G\right]
\le \frac{25\lambda(H_G)}{n}
\le C\frac{d^2}{n}.
\]
Consequently \(R_2(G)\le C d^2/n\) for every such \(G\), and in particular with probability \(1-o(1)\) over \(G_n\).  This theorem does not assert an \(O(d^2/[n\log(d+2)])\) risk bound for the capsule estimator \(\widehat\tau_G\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The capsule rate \(O(d^2/[n\log(d+2)])\) depends on the unresolved kernel bound. The proved replacement uses the published Conflict Graph Design, Rao--Blackwellizes its metadata-dependent estimator into the frozen observed-data class, and yields the valid \(O(d^2/n)\) upper bound.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Can the local handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{loc}}\) be developed into an algorithm running in time polynomial in \(n\) and \(d\) that evaluates or approximates \(\widehat\tau_G\) from \((G,Z^{\mathrm{cap}},y(Z^{\mathrm{cap}}))\), and returns an observable certificate \(U_G\) satisfying
\[
\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_2(G)}
\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau_G-\tau_G)^2\mid G]\le U_G?
\]
Can such a certificate either establish \(U_G=O(r(n,d))\) on a probability-\(1-o(1)\) random-regular graph event, or furnish a rigorous obstruction to \(\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(n/k)\), while the numerical approximation error contributes \(o(r(n,d))\)?  This is an open algorithmic and spectral question; the proved \(O(d^2/n)\) upper bound uses a different, published Conflict Graph Design.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The former certificate target assumed the unproved capsule rate and exact frontier. The revised question asks for a capsule risk certificate and explicitly leaves the logarithmic-scale spectral conclusion open, while distinguishing the different published design that supplies the proved upper bound.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove or refute the high-probability acceptance, two-sided inclusion, and \(O(n/k)\) capsule covariance bounds on a typical simple random \(d\)-regular graph.
obligation.obstruction: The opposite-arm compatible-pair block contains acceptance-conditioned weights with the random denominator \(\binom{|F_G(A)|}{k}\). Exact constant-mode cancellation in the uniform idealization does not control the heterogeneous residual operator, and an elementary Schur bound leaves an \(O(d^2)\) term.
obligation.attempted: The covariance was expanded blockwise; positive semidefiniteness, the diagonal lower bound, incompatible-pair entries, and uniform-inclusion constant-mode cancellation were proved. Diagonal, Schur, and centered radius-two spectral bounds do not remove the remaining logarithmic factor.
obligation.partial_result: The exact proved part is \(\Gamma_G=D\operatorname{Cov}(W\mid G)D\succeq0\), its arm-block decomposition, the identity \((\Gamma_G)_{uu}=\pi_u^{-1}-1\), the resulting lower bound \(\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\ge\max_u(\pi_u^{-1}-1)\), the value \(1\) on incompatible opposite-arm entries, and constant-mode cancellation when all inclusion probabilities are equal.  Thus \(n/k\) is the smallest possible norm order if \(\pi_u\asymp k/n\).  The missing result is the matching upper bound after acceptance conditioning.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Demote the unsupported capsule theorem to the directed conjecture required by the orchestrator while retaining the proved finite covariance identities.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct a polynomial-time observed-data approximation to the capsule Rao--Blackwell estimator and a valid uniform risk certificate, then determine whether it has order \(r(n,d)\) on typical random-regular graphs.
obligation.obstruction: Finite enumeration is exact but exponential, while additive entrywise Monte Carlo error does not imply the relative inclusion and operator-norm accuracy required uniformly over the endpoint \(L^2\) ball.
obligation.attempted: The task was reduced to simultaneous inclusion estimation, conditional-expectation evaluation, and covariance quadratic-form probing. Pointwise Monte Carlo handles individual queries but does not establish the required uniform relative or operator-norm error.
obligation.partial_result: The exact finite evaluator remains valid, and the proved capsule-kernel identities specify the matrix whose action must be certified; no \(O(n/k)\) upper norm estimate is presently available.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Remove the exact-frontier certificate from the downstream open question and retarget it to the unresolved capsule risk and covariance certification problem.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(c(d+1)^2/[n\log(d+2)]\le R_2(G)\le C d^2/n\) with probability \(1-o(1)\); the upper bound is attained by the published Conflict Graph Design after observed-data Rao--Blackwellization, while the corresponding logarithmic capsule bound remains open.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The prior metadata incorrectly advertised the capsule as attaining the logarithmic lower scale.

proposed.comparator_claim: For random \(d\)-regular \(G\) with \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), the published bracket is \(d/n\lesssim R_2(G)\lesssim d^2/n\) with probability \(1-o(1)\).

Lemma 3.3 gives closed-form desired-exposure probabilities, Lemma 4.2 gives the local covariance bounds, and Theorem 4.1 bounds modified Horvitz--Thompson variance by \(12.5\lambda(H_G)/n\) times the two endpoint empirical second moments after the GATE spectral identification.
The neighborhood-union construction gives a one-sided treated-component upper bound under controlled codegrees and leaves the full estimator open.
A greedy independent focal set has size at least \(n\log s/s\) with high probability in the paper's Erd\H{o}s--R\'{e}nyi regime.
Theorem 4 and Corollary 5 compare uniform root mean-squared error of a design-based Riesz estimator with the scaled norm of its variance operator.
The largest balanced independent sets in generic random bipartite graphs have density \((2+o_d(1))\log d/d\), with a factor-two local-algorithm barrier.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove or refute the high-probability acceptance, uniform inclusion, and \(O(n/k)\) covariance-operator bounds for the accepted symmetrized reservoir capsule on a typical simple random \(d\)-regular graph.
open_obligations.obstruction: The random compatible reservoir contributes weights involving \(\binom{|F_G(A)|}{k}^{-1}\). Fixed arm sizes cancel the exact constant mode only under uniform inclusion, while the heterogeneous residual is not controlled by the frozen random-regular assumptions; the Schur bound is only \(O(d^2+n/k)\).
open_obligations.attempted: The block covariance expansion, positive-semidefinite representation, diagonal lower bound, incompatible opposite-arm entries, and constant-mode cancellation were derived. Entrywise, Schur, and centered radius-two bounds all leave the logarithmic factor unresolved.
open_obligations.partial_result: The exact proved part is \(\Gamma_G=D\operatorname{Cov}(W\mid G)D\succeq0\), its arm-block decomposition, the identity \((\Gamma_G)_{uu}=\pi_u^{-1}-1\), the resulting lower bound \(\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\ge\max_u(\pi_u^{-1}-1)\), the value \(1\) on incompatible opposite-arm entries, and constant-mode cancellation when all inclusion probabilities are equal.  Thus \(n/k\) is the smallest possible norm order if \(\pi_u\asymp k/n\).  The missing result is the matching upper bound after acceptance conditioning.

prose_updates.tldr: For fixed potential outcomes under arbitrary neighborhood interference on a revealed random \(d\)-regular graph, the proved result is a logarithmic-width minimax bracket: with probability \(1-o(1)\), \(c(d+1)^2/[n\log(d+2)]\le R_2(G)\le C d^2/n\). The lower side is the preserved all-procedure theorem; the upper side follows from the published Conflict Graph Design after Rao--Blackwellization into the observed-data minimax class. The reservoir capsule has exact positive-semidefinite, diagonal, block, and constant-mode identities, but its proposed \(O(n/k)\) covariance norm and logarithmically improved risk remain open.

project_justification.gap: Published unrestricted minimax theory places random-regular full-GATE risk between \(d/n\) and \(d^2/n\). The proved all-procedure lower bound raises the lower edge to \((d+1)^2/[n\log(d+2)]\), but no proved design closes the remaining logarithmic factor.
project_justification.niche: The two-copy exposure graph and balanced reservoir capsule expose exact covariance structure that identifies the missing step: a heterogeneous compatible-pair operator bound after acceptance conditioning. This structure is retained as a directed conjecture rather than treated as an attained rate.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the strengthened all-procedure lower edge, gives a complete observed-data adaptation of the published \(O(d^2/n)\) conflict-graph upper design, derives the capsule's exact finite covariance identities, and states the resulting logarithmic-width bracket without claiming an exact frontier.

sampling_model.design: Conditional on the revealed \(G\), the proved upper guarantee uses the outcome-independent published Conflict Graph Design and an observed-data Rao--Blackwellized modified Horvitz--Thompson estimator. The capped balanced reservoir law \(\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}}\) is retained as a separate candidate whose sharper covariance rate is open.
sampling_model.units: The finite population \(V\) and its potential-outcome schedule are fixed conditional on \(G\); assignment is the only inferential randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: Both designs generate one binary assignment. The published design resolves requested endpoint exposures by a conflict-graph importance ordering; the capsule forces the closed neighborhoods of its two focal reservoirs to opposite arms and randomizes the remainder.
sampling_model.overlap: The published design's desired-exposure probabilities are explicitly positive by its closed-form Lemma 3.3. Uniform order-\(k/n\) overlap for the accepted capsule is part of the unresolved capsule conjecture and is not assumed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no super-population nuisances. Published desired-exposure weights have closed forms; capsule inclusion and Rao--Blackwell weights are exact finite-design functionals computable by enumeration, while polynomial-time uniform approximation remains open.

prose_updates.related_work: Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje define the identical endpoint-\(L^2\) unrestricted minimax experiment and prove the random-regular bracket \(d/n\lesssim R_2(G)\lesssim d^2/n\) under \(d=o(\sqrt n)\). The preserved all-procedure theorem strengthens their lower edge to order \(d^2/[n\log(d+2)]\) when \(d\to\infty\), but the upper edge remains their order. Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw provide the closed route used here: Lemma 3.3 gives exact desired-exposure probabilities, Lemma 4.2 controls local normalized covariances, and Theorem 4.1 gives the \(O(\lambda(H_G)/n)\) modified Horvitz--Thompson variance bound. Li and Li motivate neighborhood-union denominator protection but prove only a treated-component result. Harshaw, S\"avje, and Wang motivate operator-norm risk analysis, while Perkins and Wang and Cai, Zhang, and Airoldi concern balanced or independent sets in different graph and estimand settings; none supplies the acceptance-conditioned two-arm capsule covariance estimate needed to remove the logarithmic gap.
prose_updates.interpretation: The result separates what is known from what is suggested by the stable-set capsule. The all-procedure converse rules out risk below order \(d^2/[n\log d]\), whereas the best proved design guarantee is order \(d^2/n\). Exact capsule algebra shows why an \(O(n/k)\) norm would be rate-optimal for that construction, but it does not establish the required upper bound.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The unresolved step is uniform control of the accepted reservoir's heterogeneous compatible-pair covariance block. Positive semidefiniteness, diagonal scale, incompatible-pair entries, and fixed-cardinality cancellation are exact, but acceptance conditioning introduces the random denominator \(\binom{|F_G(A)|}{k}\). Entrywise or Schur bounds leave an \(O(d^2)\) contribution, so they cannot prove the desired \(O(n/k)\) norm. No covariance or switching premise is added to assume this crux.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper proves a strengthened lower edge and a published-design \(O(d^2/n)\) upper edge, not an exact minimax frontier. It does not claim that the capsule attains \(d^2/[n\log d]\), that its focal overlap is uniformly of order \(k/n\), or that a sharpened sample-size threshold has been established. Exact enumeration makes the capsule estimator total but can be exponential; scalable evaluation and certification remain open. No studentized central limit theorem, bounded-outcome model, additive interference model, or real-network random-regular approximation is claimed.

statement_notes.justification: This conjecture preserves the exact covariance identities and isolates the one operator estimate that would be needed for a sharper capsule theorem.
statement_notes.gap: No switching, mixing, or spectral argument currently controls the acceptance-conditioned compatible-pair block at order \(n/k\).
statement_notes.consumer: It is not a premise of any proved headline; it directs future work on whether the capsule can improve the published upper rate.

statement_notes.gap: Its order is \(d^2/n\), leaving a logarithmic factor above the all-procedure lower edge.
statement_notes.consumer: The logarithmic-gap bracket theorem uses it as the upper side.
